## Pull Request Submission Checklist
- [x] Follows [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/snyk/cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) guidelines
- [x] Includes detailed description of changes
- [X] Contains risk assessment (Medium)
- [ ] Highlights breaking API changes (if applicable)
- [ ] Links to automated tests covering new functionality
- [ ] Includes manual testing instructions (if necessary)
- [ ] Updates relevant GitBook documentation (PR link: ___)

## What does this PR do?

- **chore(deps): upgrade goproxy to latest**
- **fix: do not include extra certs in proxy certificate**

This change indicates that the system now only keeps the original self-signed certificate in the PEM block while still adding additional CA certificates to the certificate pool via rootCAs.AddCert(). This is a more efficient approach since:

- The proxy only needs the self-signed certificate for MITM operations
- The additional CA certificates are still available in the root CA pool for verification
- It prevents the potential OpenSSL excessive message size issue by keeping the PEM block smaller

This aligns with the behaviour [implemented in goproxy up until this change](https://github.com/elazarl/goproxy/commit/bd0b840b596f3cb67f026bdc7183447d5b0f7061#diff-382c42121d78e1b3f93f4e60409563c2e7ca0026d2ebe9bbac2105bb4f5003e0R115-L105)

## How should this be manually tested?

You will need:
- openssl available on your machine for the certificate bundle
- an opensource manifest file. An empty but valid package.json is fine. 

Instructions assume MacOS, adjust for your platform as required. 

### Original bug as seen with v1.1295.1

1. `curl --compressed https://downloads.snyk.io/cli/v1.1295.1/snyk-macos -o ~/snyk-1.1295.1`
2. `export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS='/usr/local/etc/openssl@3/cert.pem'`
3.  `~/snyk-1.1295.1 test .`
4. Observe `write EPROTO 0052E60602000000:error:0A000098:SSL routines:read_state_machine:excessive message size:../deps/openssl/openssl/ssl/statem/statem.c:621:`

### Verify the fix

1. You should have openssl available on your machine.
2. Assuming MacOS, run `export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS='/usr/local/etc/openssl@3/cert.pem'`
3. `./binary-releases/snyk-macos test .`
4. ✨ Success

Reference: CLI-658

# Frontend PR Preview & Deployment Workflow Enhancement

## Overview
This PR implements automated preview environments for frontend development and enhances the deployment workflow using GitHub Actions.

## Key Features

### 1. PR Preview Environment
- Automatically creates a preview environment for each PR and feature branch  
- Deploys to S3 with static website hosting  
- Generates unique preview URLs for easy testing  
- Automatically cleans up resources when PR is closed  

### 2. AWS Integration
- Uses OIDC for secure AWS authentication  
- Configures S3 buckets with proper public access settings  
- Implements proper bucket naming convention and validation  
- Manages bucket lifecycle (creation, configuration, cleanup)  

### 3. Notifications & Integration
- Automatically comments preview URL on PR  
- Discord notifications for:  
  - Preview environment creation  
  - Environment cleanup  
  - Build status updates  

## Technical Details

### Workflow Triggers
- Pull requests to `dev` branch  
- Push to `feature/*` branches  
- Manual trigger (`workflow_dispatch`)  

### Environment Configuration
env:
  NODE_VERSION: "22.1.0"
  PREVIEW_BUCKET_PREFIX: "pr-preview-"
  AWS_REGION: ap-southeast-2
  
  ## Security Considerations
- Implements secure AWS authentication using OIDC  
- Proper S3 bucket policies for public access  
- Managed public access controls  
- Cleanup procedures for resource management  

## Required Permissions
- S3 bucket management  
- CloudFront operations  
- GitHub OIDC integration  
- PR comment creation  

## Testing Instructions
1. Create a new PR or push to a feature branch  
2. Workflow will automatically create a preview environment  
3. Check PR comments for the preview URL  
4. Verify Discord notifications  
5. Confirm cleanup when PR is closed  

## Dependencies
- AWS S3 for static hosting  
- GitHub Actions for CI/CD  
- Discord for notifications  
- Node.js v22.1.0  

## Related Changes
- Added AWS IAM policies for preview environments  
- Configured OIDC authentication  
- Implemented automated cleanup procedures  

## Notes
- Preview URLs follow the format:  
  `http://{bucket-name}.s3-website.{region}.amazonaws.com`  
- Resources are automatically cleaned up when PRs are closed  
- Bucket names are automatically generated and validated  

## Future Improvements
- Add custom domain support for previews  
- Implement caching strategies  
- Add performance monitoring  
- Enhanced preview environment management

body:
# Implement 3D Simulation Grid with Dynamic Generation, Gravity Warping, and Live Updates

This PR improves the 3D simulation system by introducing dynamic grid generation, real-time gravity-based warping, and better camera interactions. The grid is now dynamically constructed based on the bounding box of celestial bodies and is updated continuously as the simulation progresses. Gravity effects are applied to the grid points, making them shift according to the mass distribution of nearby objects.

The new implementation ensures that the grid adapts to changes in the simulation, creating a more realistic representation of how objects interact in space. The camera system has also been refined to provide better control over zooming and focusing, allowing for a smoother navigation experience.

The update also replaces manual state polling in LiveView with event-driven updates using Phoenix PubSub. The simulation state is pushed to the client whenever a change occurs, eliminating unnecessary polling and improving performance. Instead of rendering a fixed grid, the LiveView process now listens for grid_update events and updates the client dynamically.

On the backend, a new GravityField module applies gravitational transformations to points in the simulation. The grid is generated by computing a bounding box around the celestial bodies, and its resolution can be adjusted using a configurable parameter. This ensures that the grid scales appropriately with the simulation and avoids unnecessary computational overhead.

body:
#### PR description:

This PR is the re-implementation of PR [#46977](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/46977), that was reverted by the following PR [#47115](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/47115) because of the backward compatibility issue described in detail in PR [#47114](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/issues/47114).

The new implementation of the BTLDetId class and corresponding BTLNumberingScheme features two numbering schemes that coexist. The first is identical to the old one, and it is used when running simulation in BTL geometry scenarios v2 and v3 (geometry v1 is deprecated and not available anymore), the second is the new BTLDetId, used in v4 geometry, whose features are described in PR [#46977](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/46977). From the geometric layout point of view, v4 is identical to v3, and is used just to cleanly separate the use of old and new numbering scheme.

The two versions of BTLDetIds have two different explicit constructors. A dedicated bit of the BTLDetId itself identify which version of the id is used. All methods implemented to derive the id number of a BTL partition (crystal, sensor module, detector module, readout unit, tray) work in all scenarios. The mapping of these elements are described in two separate DNs for the two cases:
[DN-23-006](https://icms.cern.ch/tools/publications/notes/entries/DN/2023/006) for geometry v2-v3, and  [DN-24-014](https://icms.cern.ch/tools/publications/notes/entries/DN/2024/014) for v4.

The new numbering scheme also introduces a mapping for the electronic components of BTL, as described in [DN-24-014](https://icms.cern.ch/tools/publications/notes/entries/DN/2024/014), valid only for the updated version of the BTLDetId and in geometry v4.

## Summary

This is a big one, here's the highlight of the changes **user face**. The changes applied to the codegen merely reflect that changes applied to the structure of the new, proposed documentation.

Closes https://github.com/biomejs/website/issues/1765
Closes https://github.com/biomejs/website/issues/1764
Closes https://github.com/biomejs/website/issues/1766
Closes https://github.com/biomejs/website/issues/1767

### Rule page

I removed the "Note" and moved all the important information inside a `## Summary` header. The information is just a bullet list. I updated this list to also account for the new domains.

### Rules and actions divided by language

Rules and actions are divided by language. Now that our infrastructure is maturing and we are spanning rules across languages, the current division of the pages isn't optimal, and people might get confused when they see multiple instances on one page. So now, the page `/linter/rules/index.mdx` doesn't exist anymore, instead is copied under each language we support: `/linter/javascript/rules/index.mdx`, `/linter/css/rules/index.mdx` and so on.

You can see the result for yourselves, because it gets **way** easier to understand when a rule is applied to specific language. Sure, the icons did help, but I believe having a dedicated page reduces the cognitive load of our users. 

### Documentation of linter groups

I removed the code generation of the linter groups. It seemed unnecessary, considering they are hardcoded. Instead, I moved the groups' documentation inside the `/linter` page. Plus, I used lowercase names so they could reflect the names we have in the configuration. 

### Revamp of the linter page

I changed the documentation of the `/linter` page:
- Removed the `## Rules` header, and all the sub-headers are now a `##` as a result
- Documented the new suppression systems we have
- Added a FAQ section at the end
- Expanded the migration guide by using the new `--suppress` CLI option that we added in v2
- Removed all the `Since ..` from the web page. I rewrote everything by assuming that we have it in v2 since we don't maintain multiple versions of Biome.

### Expressive code goodies

I added a plugin to expressive code (it required a config), which shows the line numbers of the snippets. 

I needed those line numbers to document the new suppression system of the linter. I hope it's a good addition. It's still possible to disable the line numbers *per code block*.

## What's left

Linter domains haven't been documented. I will do that in a subsequent PR. I plan to have some codegen since there is "hidden" information that we have to pull, such as the dependencies of each domain.
